title: Intermittent Omnipod Dash bolus failures — BusyException race in OmnipodDashBleManagerImpl, more pronounced on Atlas (InPlay BLE) pods
body:
## Summary

Intermittent bolus delivery failures ("Failed to send the command") with Omnipod Dash. Pod history shows repeated failures at the same timestamp followed by eventual success. The issue appears correlated with the newer Atlas (InPlay BLE) pod hardware generation versus the older SAW (TWI Board) generation, failures began within the same timeframe as switching pod stock from SAW to Atlas after running out of SAW pods.

## Root cause

In `pump/omnipod/common/src/main/kotlin/app/aaps/pump/omnipod/common/bledriver/comm/OmnipodDashBleManagerImpl.kt`, the `busy: AtomicBoolean` lock guarding `connect()`, `sendCommand()`, and `pairNewPod()` is released in a `finally { busy.set(false) }` block that executes *after* `emitter.onComplete()`. Because RxJava's `Observable.concat()` synchronously subscribes to the next source the moment `onComplete()` fires — before the `finally` block runs — a command dispatched immediately after a connection completes can observe `busy == true` and throw `BusyException` before any BLE I/O is attempted.

This explains:
- Why increasing `DEFAULT_IO_TIMEOUT_MS` from 1000ms to 2500ms had no effect (the failure occurs before any packet write, so the timeout is never reached)
- Why bolus commands fail while TBR/Cancel TBR commands at the same timestamp succeed (a failed bolus's retry loop in `waitForBolusDeliveryToComplete()` incidentally waits long enough for the original connection to finish, leaving a stable connection for the subsequent TBR)

## Why Atlas pods may be more affected

This race condition likely exists regardless of pod generation but requires a sufficiently wide timing window between BLE connection initiation and session establishment to trigger reliably. Atlas (InPlay BLE) pods may have different BLE/EAP-AKA session establishment timing than SAW (TWI Board) pods. (Note: LoopKit's iOS documentation independently describes different reconnection behavior for Atlas pods on certain iPhone models, which is suggestive though not direct confirmation of the same mechanism here.)

## Proposed fix

Move `busy.set(false)` to execute immediately before each `emitter.onComplete()` / `emitter.tryOnError()` call rather than in a trailing `finally` block, across all exit paths in `sendCommand()`, `connect()`, and `pairNewPod()`. This closes the window so no downstream subscriber can observe `busy == true` after a method has signaled completion.

A complete diff covering all identified exit paths (14 total across the three methods) is available and was validated via multi-pass static analysis. **This fix has been applied and is undergoing real-world on-body testing; results not yet confirmed.** Posting now for visibility and to invite review/testing from others, particularly those also experiencing this issue on Atlas pods.

Happy to share the full diff and analysis on request.

comments.body:
Update: Applied the proposed fix (moved busy.set(false) before 
emitter.onComplete()/tryOnError() across all exit paths in 
sendCommand(), connect(), and pairNewPod()) and tested on-body 
with Atlas pods. Bolus failures continued at the same frequency 
-- reverted the change. This rules out the BusyException ordering 
defect as the sole cause, though it may still be a contributing 
factor. Continuing to investigate.

[Google-Pixel-9-Pro-XL-Android-17_2026-06-30_132946.logcat.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29517283/Google-Pixel-9-Pro-XL-Android-17_2026-06-30_132946.logcat.txt)

## Update: Root cause identified via logcat capture (not the BLE race)

After applying and testing the BusyException ordering fix, bolus 
failures continued at the same frequency. Reverted that change. 
Captured a full logcat during a live failure event, which revealed 
a different and unrelated root cause:

java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Number of units must be dividable by 0.05
    at ProgramBolusCommand$Builder.setNumberOfUnits(ProgramBolusCommand.kt:70)

Immediately preceding this in the log:

deliverTreatment: requestedBolusAmount=0.025

## Root cause

I use U200 insulin concentration. The loop calculated an SMB of 
0.05 U (the pod's minimum deliverable amount), but the U200 
concentration conversion is halving this value to 0.025 before 
it reaches the pod command builder. The Omnipod Dash has a fixed 
minimum bolus/pulse increment of 0.05 units regardless of insulin 
concentration -- this is a hardware constraint on the pod's pulse 
mechanism, not affected by U100 vs U200. The conversion logic 
appears to be applying the U200 halving to a value that needs to 
remain a clean multiple of 0.05 for the pod to accept it.

This means any SMB or bolus amount that becomes a non-multiple of 
0.05 after U200 conversion (e.g. 0.05 -> 0.025, 0.15 -> 0.075) 
will fail at the command builder validation stage, before any BLE 
communication is attempted -- which is why this presents identically 
to a BLE failure ("Failed to send the command") but has nothing to 
do with BLE timing, connection state, or pod hardware generation.

This explains why the BusyException race fix had no effect, and 
likely explains most or all of my reported bolus failures, separate 
from the Atlas pod investigation above.
